title: Chord Length Relationships Practice
description: Practice using intersecting chord products to solve missing segment lengths.

questions.question: Two chords AB and CD intersect at P. Which equation matches the intersecting chords theorem?
questions.explanation: For intersecting chords, the product of the two segments on one chord equals the product of the two segments on the other chord: AP · PB = CP · PD.

questions.question: One chord has segments 6 and 8. The other chord has segments 4 and x. What is x?
When two chords intersect inside a circle, you multiply the two pieces on the same chord to form each product.
questions.explanation: Each product uses the two segment lengths from one chord.

questions.question: Two chords intersect. One chord has segments 9 and 4. The other chord has segments 6 and x. Enter the value of x.
Chords AB and CD intersect at P. If AP = 5, PB = 12, CP = 10, and PD = x, what is x?
A chord has total length 15. One segment is 6. What is the other segment?
questions.explanation: The whole chord is 15, so the other segment is 15 - 6 = 9.

questions.question: One chord has segments 7 and 12. The other chord has segments x and 6. What equation should you solve?
questions.explanation: The two pieces on the first chord are 7 and 12, so their product equals the product x · 6.

questions.question: Explain why the setup 8 · 3 = 4 · x is correct when one chord has segments 8 and 3 and the other has segments 4 and x.
questions.correctAnswer: The intersecting chords theorem says the product of the two segments on one chord equals the product of the two segments on the other chord, so 8 and 3 are multiplied together and set equal to 4 times x.
questions.explanation: A correct explanation should mention that each product uses the two pieces from the same chord.
